children.description: Build fails because the base image's OS has reached end-of-life, causing its package repositories to become unavailable (typically resulting in 404 errors).
Build fails because the base image's OS (e.g., Debian Stretch/Jessie, Ubuntu 14.04) has reached end-of-life, causing apt-get update to fail with 404 errors from archived or removed repositories.
Build fails due to network issues (timeouts, DNS, connection resets), repository unavailability (503 errors, deprecation), or filesystem/daemon issues preventing downloads or operations.
Build fails due to network timeouts, connection resets, EOF errors, or general unreachability preventing downloads or operations.

children.category: DNS Resolution and Host Unreachable Errors
children.description: Build fails due to DNS resolution failures, host unreachable errors, or inability to resolve repository/package server addresses.
Build fails due to server-side HTTP errors (404, 500, 502, 503, 504) from package registries, mirrors, or Docker registries.

children.category: Repository Authentication and Key Retrieval Failures
children.description: Build fails due to authentication failures (e.g., HTTP 401/403) or inability to fetch GPG keys from keyservers.
Build fails because a package repository, registry, or mirror is temporarily unavailable or unreachable, causing unsatisfiable constraints.
Build fails due to SSL certificate verification failures when downloading resources over HTTPS.
Build fails because of expired, missing, or invalid SSL/TLS certificates or CA bundles, preventing secure connections to repositories or registries.
Build fails due to package manager errors such as unmet dependencies, version conflicts, or packages missing from the repository.
Build fails because a specified package version is incompatible, conflicts with other dependencies, or is not available in the repository.
Build fails because a specified package name is incorrect, misspelled, or the package is missing from the configured source.
Build fails due to missing system-level libraries, development headers, or tools required for package installation or compilation.
Build fails due to network issues, corrupted downloads, or integrity checksum mismatches during package fetch.
Build fails because a package or tool requires a newer or different version of the language runtime or compiler than is installed.
Build fails due to errors in the build environment, such as syntax errors in scripts, unsupported package builds, or compatibility issues with the build tools.

Build fails due to incompatibility between the installed version of a language runtime (e.g., Go, Node.js, Ruby, Python) or tool (e.g., npm, Bundler) and the requirements of a dependency or the project.
Build fails because the system's package manager (e.g., apk, pip) blocks direct installations to prevent conflicts with system-managed packages, often on Alpine Linux.
Build fails during the compilation or building of a specific dependency due to missing components, unsupported build backends (e.g., PEP 517), deprecated configurations, or package structure issues.
Build fails due to issues with the package manager itself (e.g., npm 'cb() never called!', corrupted tarballs) or its interaction with the package registry.
Build fails due to syntax errors, formatting issues, or unsupported script formats in build scripts or package postinstall scripts.
Build fails due to file system conflicts, such as attempting to copy files to a path that already exists as a non-directory.
Build fails due to conflicts in file or directory paths, such as COPY/ADD destination conflicts, npm cache corruption, or node_modules conflicts from host copy.
Build fails because a required command or executable (e.g., npm) is not found in the current environment or PATH.
Build fails because a required command, executable, package manager, build tool, compiler, or script is missing from the environment or PATH.
